paragraphs: BJ's Wholesale Club is a leading operator of membership warehouse clubs concentrated primarily in the eastern half of the United States. We deliver significant value to our members, consistently offering up to 25% savings on a representative basket of manufacturer-branded groceries compared to traditional supermarket competitors. We provide a curated assortment focused on groceries, fresh foods, general merchandise, gasoline, and other ancillary services to deliver a differentiated shopping experience that is further enhanced by our digital capabilities. Additionally, we provide access to coupons and promotions to deliver further value to our members.

Since pioneering the warehouse club model in New England in 1984, we have grown our footprint to 263 large-format, high volume warehouse clubs and 199 gas stations spanning 21 states as of fiscal year end 2025. In our originating New England market, which has high population density and generates a disproportionate part of U.S. gross domestic product ("GDP"), we operate nearly three times the number of clubs compared to the next largest warehouse club competitor. In addition to shopping in our clubs, members are able to shop when and how they want through our website, bjs.com, and our highly rated mobile app, which allows them to use our buy-online-pickup-in-club ("BOPIC") service, curbside delivery, same-day delivery or traditional ship-to-home service, as well as through the DoorDash and Instacart marketplaces. We also offer Same-Day Select, which offers BJ's members the ability to pay a one-time fee for unlimited same-day deliveries over a one-year period. Additionally, members may use ExpressPay® to skip checkout lines when they shop in club and pay via their mobile devices.

Our goal is to offer our members significant value and a meaningful return in savings on their annual membership fee. We have over 8 million members paying annual fees to gain access to savings on groceries, general merchandise, services, and gasoline. The annual membership fee for our Club membership is generally $60 and the annual membership fee for our Club+ membership, which offers additional value-enhancing features, is generally $120. Prior to January 1, 2025, the Club and Club+ membership fees were $55 and $110 per year, respectively. We believe that members can save over ten times their $60 Club membership fee versus what they would otherwise pay at traditional supermarket competitors when they spend $2,500 or more per year at BJ's on manufacturer-branded groceries. In addition to providing significant savings on a representative basket of manufacturer-branded groceries, we accept all manufacturer coupons and also carry our own exclusive brands that enable members to save on price without compromising on quality. Our two private label brands, Wellsley Farms® and Berkley Jensen®, represent approximately 27% of our total net sales, excluding gasoline. Our customers recognize the relevance of our value proposition across economic environments, as demonstrated by over 25 consecutive years of membership fee income growth. Our membership fee income was $499.8 million for fiscal year 2025.

Warehouse clubs offer a relatively narrow assortment of food and general merchandise items within a wide range of product categories. In order to achieve high sales volumes and rapid inventory turnover, merchandise selections are generally limited to items that are brand name leaders in their categories, alongside an assortment of private label brands. Since warehouse clubs sell a diversified selection of product categories, they attract customers from a wide range of other wholesale and retail distribution channels, such as supermarkets, supercenters, online retailers, gasoline stations, hard discounters, department and specialty stores, and operators selling a single category or narrow range of merchandise. Traditionally, these higher cost distribution channels have been unable to match the value proposition offered by warehouse clubs over extended periods of time.

Warehouse clubs eliminate, or significantly reduce, many of the merchandise handling costs associated with traditional multiple-step distribution channels, such as distributors' commissions and the cost of storing merchandise in central distribution facilities, by purchasing large quantities of merchandise directly from manufacturers and storing merchandise on the sales floor. The operation of no-frills, self-service warehouse facilities creates freight volume and handling efficiencies, allowing for operating costs which are substantially below those of traditional retailers. Because of their higher sales volumes and rapid inventory turnover, warehouse clubs generate cash from the sale of a large portion of their inventory before they are required to pay merchandise vendors. As a result, much of the inventory is financed through vendor payment terms rather than working capital. Two broad groups of customers, individual households and small businesses, have been attracted to the savings made possible by the high sales volumes and operating efficiencies achieved by warehouse clubs. Customers at warehouse clubs are generally limited to members who pay an annual fee.

As of January 31, 2026, we operated 263 clubs ranging in size from 44,000 square feet to 177,000 square feet. We aim to build our large format clubs in locations with high density and high traffic, which are visible to and convenient for our members. We design our smaller format clubs to serve markets with a population that is likely insufficient to support a large format club, or in locations where there is inadequate real estate space for a large format club, such as urban areas. Including space for parking, the amount of land required to develop a BJ's club generally ranges from ten acres to fourteen acres. Our clubs are located in both free-standing locations and shopping centers.

Our ability to achieve profitable operations depends upon high sales volumes and the efficient operation of our warehouse clubs. We procure most of our merchandise directly from manufacturers and route it to distribution centers or directly to our clubs. Our Company-operated distribution centers receive large shipments from manufacturers and quickly ship these goods to individual clubs, generally within 24 hours. We work closely with manufacturers to minimize the amount of handling required once merchandise is received at a club. Merchandise for sale is generally displayed on pallets containing large quantities of each item, thereby reducing the labor required for handling, stocking, and restocking. Back-up merchandise is generally stored in steel racks above the sales floor.

Our operations are primarily retail club and other sales procured from clubs and distribution centers, representing one operating segment. All of our identifiable assets are located in the United States. We do not have significant sales outside of the United States, nor does any customer represent more than 10% of total revenues for any period presented.

We service our existing members and attract new members by providing a broad range of high quality, brand name and private label merchandise at prices that are consistently lower than traditional retailers, including discount retailers, supermarkets, supercenters, and specialty retail operations. We limit the items offered in each product line to fast-selling styles, sizes and colors. We may add additional temporary merchandise offerings from time to time to keep up with demand. We work
closely with manufacturers to develop packaging and sizes that are best suited for selling through the warehouse club format in order to minimize handling costs and ensure value to our members.

headings: Risks Relating to Our Business
Our business may be affected by macroeconomic and other market issues that affect consumer spending.
We depend on having a large and loyal membership, and any harm to our relationship with our members could have a material adverse effect on our business, net sales and results of operations.
Our business plan and operating results depend on our ability to procure the merchandise we sell at the best possible prices.
We depend on vendors to supply us with quality merchandise at the right time and at the right price.
Competition may adversely affect our profitability.

Changes in laws related to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program ("SNAP"), to the governmental administration of SNAP or to SNAP's EBT systems could adversely impact our results of operations.
Natural disasters, extreme weather or unusual conditions and catastrophic events beyond our control could negatively affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Disruptions in our merchandise distribution could adversely affect sales and member satisfaction.
We may not timely identify or respond effectively to consumer trends, which could negatively affect our relationship with our members, the demand for our products and services and our market share.
We are subject to payment-related risks, including risks to the security of payment card information.
Our co-branded credit card program may be affected by economic and regulatory conditions.

We rely extensively on information technology to process transactions, compile results and manage our businesses. Failure or disruption of our primary and back-up systems could adversely affect our businesses.
If we do not successfully maintain a relevant digital experience for our members, our results of operations could be adversely impacted.
Global or regional pandemics, epidemics or outbreaks of infectious disease, could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Union attempts to organize our team members could disrupt our business.
Our comparable club sales and quarterly operating results may fluctuate significantly.
Changes in our product mix or in our revenues from gasoline sales could negatively impact our revenue and results of operations.
Product recalls could adversely affect our sales and results of operations.
We depend on the financial performance of our operations in the New York metropolitan area.
Our growth strategy to open new clubs involves risks.
Because we compete to a substantial degree on price, changes affecting the market prices of the goods we sell could adversely affect our net sales and operating profit.
Any harm to the reputation of our private label brands could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations.
We may not be able to protect our intellectual property adequately, which, in turn, could harm the value of our brand and adversely affect our business.

Our business is moderately seasonal and weak performance during one of our historically strong seasonal periods could have a material adverse effect on our operating results for the entire fiscal year.
Implementation of technology initiatives could disrupt our operations in the near term and fail to provide the anticipated benefits.
Inventory shrinkage could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
We are subject to risks associated with leasing substantial amounts of space.
We are subject to a number of risks because we import some of our merchandise.
Because of our international sourcing, we could be adversely affected by violations of the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and similar worldwide anti-bribery and anti-kickback laws.

Changes in accounting standards and subjective assumptions, estimates and judgments by management related to complex accounting matters could significantly affect our financial condition and results of operations.
Goodwill and identifiable intangible assets represent a significant portion of our total assets, and any impairment of these assets could adversely affect our results of operations.
We are a holding company with no operations of our own, and we depend on our subsidiaries for cash.
paragraphs: Set forth below are the risks that we believe are material to our investors and they should be carefully considered. These risks are not all of the risks that we face and other factors not presently known to us or that we currently believe are immaterial may also affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and/or stock price if they occur. This section contains forward-looking statements. You should refer to the explanation of the qualifications and limitations on forward-looking statements in the Forward-Looking Statements section above and should also refer to our quarterly reports on Form 10-Q and current reports on Form 8-K for any material updates to these risk factors.

Our results of operations are affected by the level of consumer spending and, therefore, by changes in the economic factors that impact consumer spending. Certain economic conditions or events, such as a contraction in the financial markets; high rates of inflation or deflation; high unemployment levels; decreases in consumer disposable income; unavailability of consumer credit; higher consumer debt levels; higher tax rates and other changes in tax laws; fluctuations in interest rates; decreased consumer confidence, higher fuel, energy and other commodity costs; weakness in the housing market; higher insurance and health care costs; and product cost increases resulting from an increase in commodity prices or supply chain issues, could reduce, and in some cases have reduced, consumer spending generally, which could cause our customers to spend less or to shift their spending to our competitors. Reduced consumer spending may result in reduced demand for our items and may also require increased selling and promotional expenses. Issues or trends that affect consumer spending broadly could affect spending by our members disproportionately. A reduction or shift in consumer spending could negatively impact our business, results of operations and financial condition.

We depend on having a large and loyal membership. The extent to which we achieve growth in our membership base and sustain high renewal rates materially influences our profitability. Further, our net sales are directly affected by the number of our members, the number of members and holders of our co-branded credit cards, the frequency with which our members shop at our clubs and the amount they spend on those trips, which means the loyalty and enthusiasm of our members directly impacts our net sales and operating income. Accordingly, anything that would harm our relationship with our members and lead to lower membership renewal rates or reduced spending by members in our clubs could materially adversely affect our net sales, membership fee income and results of operations.

Factors that could adversely affect our relationship with our members include: our failure to remain competitive in our pricing relative to our competitors; our failure to provide the expected quality of merchandise; our failure to offer the mix of products that our members want to purchase; events that harm our reputation or the reputation of our private brands; our failure to provide the convenience that our members may expect over time, including with respect to technology, delivery and physical location of our clubs; increases to our membership fees; and increased competition from stores, clubs or internet retailers that have a more attractive mix of price, quality and convenience. In addition, we constantly need to attract new members to replace our members who fail to renew and to grow our membership base. If we fail to attract new members, our membership fee income and net sales could suffer.

Our business plan depends on our ability to procure the merchandise we sell at the best possible prices. Because we price our merchandise aggressively, the difference between the price at which we sell a given item and the cost at which we purchase it is often much smaller than it would be for our non-club competitors. Further, it is often not possible for us to reflect increases in our cost of goods by increasing our prices to members. Accordingly, small changes in the prices at which we purchase our goods for resale can have a substantial impact on our operating profits. If we are unable to purchase goods at attractive prices relative to our competitors, our growth could suffer. If the prices we pay for goods increase, our operating profit and results of operations could suffer, and if we are forced to increase our prices to our members, our member loyalty could suffer.

We depend heavily on our ability to purchase merchandise in sufficient quantities at competitive prices and in a timely fashion. We source our merchandise from a wide variety of domestic and international vendors. Finding qualified vendors who meet our standards and acquiring merchandise in a timely and efficient manner are significant challenges, especially with respect to vendors located and merchandise sourced outside the United States. We have no assurances of continued supply, pricing or access to new products, and, in general, any vendor could at any time change the terms upon which it sells to us or discontinue selling to us. In addition, member demand may lead to insufficient in-stock quantities of our merchandise. Additionally, if a significant vendor, particularly a vendor that supplies high demand products and for which we have limited alternative sources, has a supply chain disruption for any reason that negatively impacts their ability to supply us with the products we need in a timely or cost-effective manner, such disruption could have, and in the past has had, a material impact on our sales and results of operations.

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis is intended to promote understanding of the results of operations and financial condition of the Company and is provided as a supplement to, and should be read in conjunction with, our audited consolidated financial statements and related notes thereto included in Item 8. in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. The following discussion contains forward-looking statements that reflect our plans, estimates and assumptions. Our actual results could differ
materially from those discussed in the forward-looking statements. Factors that could cause such differences are discussed in "Item 1A. Risk Factors".

We report on the basis of a 52- or 53-week fiscal year, which ends on the Saturday closest to January 31. Accordingly, references herein to "fiscal year 2025" and "fiscal year 2024" relate to the 52 weeks ended January 31, 2026 and February 1, 2025, respectively, and references herein to "fiscal year 2023" relate to the 53 weeks ended February 3, 2024.

Our business is subject to some seasonality. Historically, our business has generally realized a slightly higher portion of net sales and cash flows from operations in the second and fourth fiscal quarters, attributable primarily to the impact of the summer and year-end holiday season, respectively. Our quarterly results have been, and will continue to be, affected by the timing of new club openings and their associated pre-opening expenses. As a result of these factors, our financial results for any single quarter or for periods of less than a year are not necessarily indicative of the results that may be achieved for a full fiscal year.

The overall economic environment and related changes in consumer behavior have a significant impact on our business. In general, positive conditions in the broader economy promote customer spending in our clubs, while economic weakness, which generally results in a reduction of customer spending, may have a different or more extreme effect on spending at our clubs. Macroeconomic factors that can affect customer spending patterns, and thereby our results of operations, include, among others, employment rates, changes to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), government stimulus programs, tax legislation, business conditions, changes in the housing market, the availability of credit, interest rates and inflation, tariffs, tax rates, and fuel and energy costs. In addition, unemployment rates and benefits may cause us to experience higher labor costs.

The membership model is a critical element of our business. Members drive our results of operations through their membership fee income and their purchases. The majority of members renew within six months following their renewal date. Therefore, our renewal rate is a trailing calculation that captures renewals during the period seven to eighteen months prior to the reporting date. We have grown our membership fee income each year for over 25 consecutive years and the quality of our membership mix is strong as evidenced by our higher tier penetration growth in fiscal year 2025. Our membership fee income totaled $499.8 million in fiscal year 2025. Our tenured membership renewal rate, a key indicator of membership engagement, satisfaction, and loyalty, was 90% at the end of fiscal year 2025.
Effective sourcing and distribution of products and consumer demands

Our net sales and gross profit are affected by our ability to purchase our products in sufficient quantities at competitive prices. Further, our ability to maintain our appeal to existing customers and attract new customers primarily depends on our ability to originate, develop, and offer a compelling product assortment responsive to customer preferences. As a result, our level of net sales could be adversely affected due to constraints in our supply chain, including our inability to procure and stock sufficient quantities of some merchandise in a manner that is able to match market demand from our customers.

Our historical operating results reflect the impact of our ongoing investments to support our growth. We have made significant investments in our business that we believe have laid the foundation for continued profitable growth. We believe that expanding our club footprint, bringing substantially all of our end-to-end perishable supply chain in-house, enhancing our information systems, including our distribution center and transportation management systems, and investing in hardware, software, and digitally enabled shopping capabilities for convenience, such as BOPIC, curbside pickup, same-day delivery, ExpressPay, and a digital coupon gallery will enable us to replicate our profitable club format and provide a differentiated shopping experience. We expect these infrastructure investments to support our successful operating model across our club operations.

The market price of gasoline impacts our net sales and comparable club sales, and large fluctuations in the price of gasoline may produce a short-term impact on our sales and margins. Retail gasoline prices are driven by daily crude oil and wholesale commodity market changes and are volatile, as they are influenced by factors that include changes in demand and supply of oil and refined products, global geopolitical events, regional market conditions, and supply interruptions caused by severe weather conditions. Typically, the change in crude oil prices impacts the purchase price of wholesale petroleum fuel products, which in turn impacts retail gasoline prices at the pump. During times when prices are particularly volatile, differences in pricing and procurement strategies between the Company and its competitors may lead to temporary margin contraction or expansion, depending on whether prices are rising or falling, and this impact could affect our overall results for a fiscal quarter.

In addition, the relative level of gasoline prices from period to period may lead to differences in our net sales between those periods. Further, because we generally attempt to maintain a fairly stable gross profit per gallon, this variance in net sales, which may be substantial, may or may not have a significant impact on our operating income.

paragraphs: BJ's Wholesale Club 是美國東部地區主要的會員制倉儲俱樂部經營者。我們為會員提供顯著的價值，持續提供比傳統超市競爭對手高達 25% 的節省，針對製造商品牌商品的代表性購物籃。我們提供精心策劃的商品組合，包括食品、新鮮食品、一般商品、汽油及其他附加服務，以提供差異化的購物體驗，並透過我們的數位能力進一步提升。此外，我們提供折扣券與促銷活動，以進一步為會員創造價值。

自 1984 年在新英格蘭地區開創倉儲俱樂部模式以來，我們已擴展至 263 家大型格式、高流量倉儲俱樂部與 199 家加油站，遍及 21 個州，截至 2025 年財務年度結算日。在我們起源的新英格蘭市場，該地區人口密度高，並產生美國國民生產總值（"GDP"）不成比例的份額，我們經營的俱樂部數量幾乎是第二大倉儲俱樂部競爭對手的三倍。除了在俱樂部內購物，會員也能透過我們的網站 bjs.com 及我們評價極高的行動應用程式進行購物，並使用我們的線上購物、俱樂部取貨（"BOPIC"）、車邊配送、隔日配送或傳統宅配服務，以及透過 DoorDash 和 Instacart 市場。我們也提供 Same-Day Select，讓 BJ's 會員支付一次性費用，即可在一年內無限次使用隔日配送服務。此外，會員也可使用 ExpressPay® 來跳過結帳排隊，並透過行動裝置付款。

我們的目標是為會員提供顯著的價值，並在年度會費上創造實質的節省回報。我們擁有超過 800 萬名會員，支付年度會費以獲得在食品、一般商品、服務及汽油上的折扣。我們俱樂部會員的年度會費通常為 $60，而俱樂部 Plus 會員的年度會費，因其提供額外價值增強功能，通常為 $120。在 2025 年 1 月 1 日之前，俱樂部與俱樂部 Plus 的會費分別為每年 $55 與 $110。我們相信，會員在每年於 BJ's 花費 $2,500 或更多於製造商品牌食品時，所節省的金額將超過其 $60 俱樂部會費的十倍。除了提供針對製造商品牌商品的代表性購物籃顯著節省，我們也接受所有製造商折扣券，並擁有我們自己的獨家品牌，使會員能在不犧牲品質的情況下節省價格。我們的兩個自有品牌 Wellsley Farms® 與 Berkley Jensen®，約佔我們總淨銷售額的 27%，不計汽油。我們的客戶認可我們價值提案在不同經濟環境中的相關性，這也體現在連續 25 年以上的會費收入成長。我們的會費收入在 2025 年財務年度為 $499.8 億。

倉儲俱樂部提供較窄的商品組合，涵蓋食品與一般商品，但範圍廣泛的產品類別。為了達到高銷售量與快速存貨週轉，商品選擇通常限於其類別中的品牌領導者，以及一些自有品牌組合。由於倉儲俱樂部銷售多樣化的產品類別，因此吸引來自其他 Wholesale 與零售分銷渠道的客戶，例如超市、超級中心、線上零售商、加油站、折扣商店、百貨與專業商店，以及銷售單一類別或窄範圍商品的經營者。傳統上，這些高成本的分銷渠道在長時間內無法與倉儲俱樂部提供的價值提案相抗衡。

倉儲俱樂部消除，或大幅降低，與傳統多層次分銷渠道相關的許多商品處理成本，例如經銷商佣金與在中央分銷中心存放商品的成本，透過直接從製造商大量採購商品並在銷售場地存放商品來實現。無繁瑣服務的自服務倉儲設施的運作，創造出運輸量與處理效率，使營運成本遠低於傳統零售商。由於銷售量高與快速存貨週轉，倉儲俱樂部能在支付商品供應商之前，即從銷售大量商品中產生現金。因此，許多存貨是透過供應商付款條件來資金融通，而非營運資金。兩個主要的客戶羣體，個人家庭與小型企業，因倉儲俱樂部所達成的高銷售量與營運效率而被吸引。倉儲俱樂部的客戶通常限於支付年度會費的會員。

截至 2026 年 1 月 31 日，我們經營 263 傢俱樂部，規模從 44,000 平方英尺至 177,000 平方英尺不等。我們致力於在人口密度高與人流量大的地區建設大型格式俱樂部，這些地區對會員而言視覺上易見且便利。我們設計較小規模的俱樂部，以服務人口不足以支持大型俱樂部的市場，或是在缺乏足夠土地空間建設大型俱樂部的地區，例如都市地區。包括停車空間，開發 BJ's 俱樂部所需的土地範圍通常為十英畝至十四英畝。我們的俱樂部位於獨立地點與購物中心內。

我們實現盈利運作的能力取決於高銷售量與俱樂部運作的效率。我們大多數商品直接從製造商採購，並運送到分銷中心或直接到俱樂部。我們公司運營的分銷中心接收大量來自製造商的貨物，並迅速將這些商品運送到各個俱樂部，通常在 24 小時內完成。我們與製造商密切合作，以減少商品到達俱樂部後所需的處理量。待售商品通常以貨架形式展示，每種商品大量存放，從而減少處理、上架與補貨所需的勞動力。備用商品通常存放在銷售場地上方的鋼架上。
截至 2026 年 1 月 31 日，我們俱樂部在各州的分佈情況如下表所示：
紐約 50 佛羅裏達 43 麻薩諸塞 26 新澤西 24 賓州 19 維吉尼亞 14 康乃狄克 13
馬裏蘭 12 北卡羅來納 11 俄亥俄 8 佐治亞 7 新罕布夏 7 田納西 6 密歇根 5 特拉華 4
羅德島 4 緬因 3 南卡羅來納 3 印第安納 2 阿拉巴馬 1 肯塔基 1 分部
本公司業務主要為零售俱樂部及其他銷售，由俱樂部及配送中心取得，代表一個應報告分部。所有可辨識資產均位於美國。本公司並無重大銷售來自美國以外地區，亦無任何客戶在任一呈列期間內代表超過 10% 的總營業收入。
本公司透過提供廣泛的高品質、品牌商品及自有品牌商品，以價格持續低於傳統零售業者（包括折扣零售業者、超級市場、超級中心及專業零售運作），服務現有會員並吸引新會員。本公司在每一系列商品中限制所提供的商品種類，僅包含快速銷售的款式、尺寸及顏色。本公司有時會增加額外的臨時商品種類，以配合需求。本公司與製造商密切合作，開發最適合透過倉庫俱樂部格式銷售的包裝及尺寸，以降低處理成本並確保對會員的價值。
closely with manufacturers to develop packaging and sizes that are best suited for selling through the warehouse club format in order to minimize handling costs and ensure value to our members.

paragraphs: 以下討論與分析旨在促進對本公司營運成果與財務狀況的瞭解，並作為對應年度報告表10-K中第8項所載經審計之合併財務報表及其相關附註的補充，應與其一併閱讀。以下討論包含前瞻性陳述，反映本公司計畫、預估與假設。本公司實際結果可能與前瞻性陳述中所討論者有所差異
與前瞻性陳述中所討論者有重大差異的因素除了上述因素外，尚有其他因素，這些因素在「第1A項 風險因素」中進行討論。
本公司以52週或53週的財務年度為基礎進行會計，財務年度結算日為距離1月31日最近的星期六。因此， herein 所提及的「財務年度2025」及「財務年度2024」分別指2026年1月31日結算的52週及2025年2月1日結算的52週，而 herein 所提及的「財務年度2023」則指2024年2月3日結算的53週。
BJ's Wholesale Club 是美國東部地區主要的會員倉儲俱樂部經營者。我們為會員提供顯著價值，持續提供比傳統超市競爭對手高達25%的製造商品牌食品折扣。我們提供經過篩選的商品組合，專注於食品、新鮮食品、一般商品、汽油及其他附加服務，以提供差異化的購物體驗，並透過我們的數位能力進一步提升。此外，我們提供折扣券與促銷活動，以進一步為會員創造價值。

自1984年在新英格蘭地區開創倉儲俱樂部模式以來，我們已擴展至263家大型格式、高流量倉儲俱樂部及199家加油站，遍及21個州。在我們起源的新英格蘭市場，該市場人口密度高，產生美國GDP的不成比例部分，我們經營的俱樂部數量幾乎是第二大倉儲俱樂部競爭對手的三倍。除了在俱樂部購物外，會員可透過我們的網站 bjs.com 及我們評價極佳的行動應用程式進行購物，該應用程式允許會員使用 BOPIC 服務、車道外送、當日送達或傳統門寄件服務，亦可透過 DoorDash 和 Instacart 市場進行購物。我們也提供 Same-Day Select 服務，讓 BJ's 會員支付一次性費用，可在一年內無限次當日送達。此外，會員可使用 ExpressPay® 服務，在俱樂部購物時跳過結帳排隊，並透過行動設備付款。

我們的目標是為會員提供顯著價值及年度會費的實質節省。我們擁有超過800萬名會員，支付年度會費以獲得食品、一般商品、服務及汽油的折扣。我們俱樂部會員的年度會費一般為60美元，俱樂部+會員的年度會費，該會員提供額外價值增強功能，一般為120美元。在2025年1月1日之前，俱樂部及俱樂部+會員的年度會費分別為55美元及110美元。我們相信，會員在BJ's 每年花費2,500美元或更多於製造商品牌食品時，可節省超過其60美元俱樂部會費十倍的費用，相較於傳統超市競爭對手。除了提供製造商品牌食品代表性購物籃的顯著折扣外，我們接受所有製造商折扣券，並擁有自有獨家品牌，使會員可在不影響品質的情況下節省價格。我們的兩個自有品牌 Wellsley Farms® 和 Berkley Jensen®，約佔我們總淨銷售額（不含汽油）的27%。我們的客戶認同我們價值主張在不同經濟環境中的相關性，如超過25年的連續會員費收入成長所顯示。我們的會員費收入在財務年度2025為499.8千萬美元。
本公司業務具有一些季節性。歷來，我們的業務通常在第二及第四財務季度實現較高的淨銷售額及營運現金流，主要歸因於夏季及年底節日季節的影響。我們的季度結果已受到新俱樂部開幕時間及其相關開幕前費用的影響，並將持續受到這些因素的影響。因此，任何單一財務季度或少於一年期間的財務結果，並不一定反映全年財務結果。

總體經濟環境及相關消費行為的變化對我們的業務有重大影響。總體而言，較佳的經濟條件會促進客戶在俱樂部的消費，而經濟疲軟，通常導致客戶消費減少，可能對我們俱樂部的消費產生不同或更極端的影響。影響客戶消費模式，進而影響我們營運成果的總體經濟因素包括，但不限於就業率、補充營養協助計畫（SNAP）的變動、政府刺激計畫、稅收立法、商業條件、住宅市場的變化、信貸的可得性、利率與通貨膨脹、關稅、稅率及燃料與能源成本。此外，失業率與福利可能導致我們面臨更高的勞動成本。

會員制度為本公司業務的重要組成部分。會員透過其會費收入及購買行為驅動本公司營運成果。大多數會員在續約日期後六個月內完成續約。因此，本公司續約率為一項追蹤計算，反映在報告日期前七至十八個月內的續約情況。本公司已連續25年以上每年成長會費收入，且會員結構品質強勁，如財務年度2025年高階會員佔比成長所顯示。本公司會費收入在財務年度2025年總計為4.998億美元。本公司會員續約率（為衡量會員參與度、滿意度及忠誠度的關鍵指標）在財務年度2025年期末為90%。
產品有效來源與分銷及消費者需求
本公司淨銷售額與毛利率受本公司能否以具競爭力價格購足產品之影響。此外，本公司能否維持現有客戶的吸引力並吸引新客戶，主要取決於本公司能否開發、推出符合客戶偏好的產品組合。因此，本公司淨銷售額可能因供應鏈限制而受到不利影響，包括本公司無法以符合市場需求的方式採購並儲存某些商品之情形。

本公司歷史營運成果反映本公司持續投資以支持成長之影響。本公司已對業務進行重大投資，並相信這些投資已為持續獲利成長奠定基礎。本公司相信擴展俱樂部據點、將絕大多數的易腐供應鏈納入本公司內部、強化資訊系統（包括配送中心與運輸管理系統），以及投資硬體、軟體及便利性數位購物功能（如BOPIC、臨時取貨、隔日達、ExpressPay及數位優惠券畫廊），將使本公司能複製獲利的俱樂部模式並提供差異化的購物體驗。本公司預期這些基礎建設投資將支持本公司在俱樂部營運中的成功營運模式。

汽油價格影響本公司淨銷售額與可比俱樂部銷售額，且汽油價格大幅波動可能對本公司銷售與毛利率產生短期影響。零售汽油價格受每日原油與批發商品市場變動所影響，且因受到油與精煉產品供需變化、全球地緣政治事件、區域市場條件及因嚴重天氣條件所導致的供應中斷等因素影響而具有不穩定性。通常，原油價格變動會影響批發石油燃料產品的購入價格，進而影響零售汽油泵站價格。在價格特別波動時期，本公司與競爭對手之間的價格與採購策略差異，可能導致暫時性毛利率收縮或擴張，視價格是上漲或下跌而定，此影響可能影響本公司整體財務季度結果。
此外，各期間汽油價格相對水平可能導致本公司各期間淨銷售額產生差異。進一步而言，因本公司通常試圖維持每加侖毛利相對穩定，此淨銷售額變動（可能相當顯著）可能對本公司營運收入產生或不產生重大影響。

headings: 與我們業務相關的風險
我們的業務可能受總體經濟及其他市場問題的影響，而這些問題會影響消費者支出。
我們依賴擁有大量且忠誠的會員，若我們與會員的關係受到損害，可能會對我們的業務、淨銷售額及營運成果造成重大不利影響。
我們的業務計畫及營運成果取決於我們能否以最佳價格取得所銷售的商品。
我們依賴供應商在正確的時間以正確的價格提供我們具品質的商品。
競爭可能對我們的利潤率產生不利影響。
與補助糧食計劃（"SNAP"）相關的法律變更，或與政府執行SNAP或SNAP的電子紅利系統（EBT）相關的法律變更，可能會對我們的營運成果產生不利影響。
天然災害、極端天氣或異常情況以及我們無法控制的災難性事件，可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生負面影響。
我方商品流通遭受到幹擾，可能對銷售及會員滿意度造成不利影響。
我方可能無法及時識別或有效回應消費者趨勢，這可能會對我方與會員的關係、產品與服務的需求以及市場佔有率造成負面影響。
我方面臨與付款相關的風險，包括支付卡資訊安全的風險。
我方聯名信用卡計劃可能受到經濟與法規環境的影響。
我方高度依賴資訊科技來處理交易、彙整結果及管理業務。主要系統或備援系統的故障或中斷，可能對我方業務造成不利影響。
若我方無法成功維持對會員而言相關的數位體驗，我方營運成果可能受到不利影響。
全球或區域性的疫情、傳染病或傳染性疾病爆發，可能對我方業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成不利影響。
工會嘗試組織我方員工，可能幹擾我方業務。
本公司之可比俱樂部銷售額及每季營運成果可能有顯著波動。
本公司產品組成之變動或來自汽油銷售之收入變動，可能對本公司營業收入及營運成果產生負面影響。
產品回收事件可能對本公司銷售額及營運成果產生負面影響。
本公司依賴紐約都會區之營運財務表現。
本公司開設新俱樂部之成長策略涉及風險。
由於本公司在價格方面競爭激烈，影響本公司所銷售商品之市場價格變動，可能對本公司淨銷售額及營運獲利產生負面影響。
本公司自有品牌之聲譽受損，可能對本公司營運成果產生重大負面影響。
本公司可能無法充分保護智慧財產權，此情形可能損害本公司品牌價值，並對本公司業務產生負面影響。
本公司業務具有中等程度之季節性，若在歷史上表現強勁之季節期間表現不佳，可能對本公司整年度之營運成果產生重大不利影響。
技術方案之實施可能在近期內幹擾本公司營運，並未能提供預期之效益。
存貨虧損可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大不利影響。
本公司面臨因租賃大量空間而產生之風險。
本公司因進口部分商品，而面臨多項風險。
由於本公司國際採購，可能因違反美國外國腐敗行為防治法及類似全球反賄賂與反回扣法規而遭受不利影響。
會計準則之變更及管理階層對複雜會計事項之主觀假設、估計與判斷，可能對本公司財務狀況及營運成果產生重大影響。
商譽及可辨認之無形資產佔本公司總資產之重大比例，若這些資產發生減值，可能對本公司營運成果產生不利影響。
本公司為一間控股公司，本身無任何營運活動，並依賴子公司提供現金。
paragraphs: 下列為我們認為對投資人具重大影響之風險，應謹慎考量。這些風險並非我們所面臨之全部風險，且其他未為我們所知或目前認為不具重大影響之因素，亦可能影響我們之業務、財務狀況、營運成果及/或股票價格，若該等因素發生。本節包含前瞻性陳述。您應參閱上文「前瞻性陳述」部分對前瞻性陳述之限制與條件說明，並應參閱我們之季報（Form 10-Q）及現況報告（Form 8-K）以取得這些風險因素之任何重大更新資訊。

我們之營運成果受消費者支出水準影響，因此亦受影響消費者支出之經濟因素變化。某些經濟條件或事件，例如金融市場收縮；高通貨膨脹或通貨緊縮率；高失業率；消費者可支配所得減少；消費者信貸不可取得；消費者負債水準提高；稅率提高及其他稅法變動；利率波動；消費者信心下降；燃料、能源及其他商品成本提高；住宅市場疲軟；保險及醫療成本提高；以及因商品價格提高或供應鏈問題導致之產品成本提高，可能減少，且在某些情況下已減少，消費者支出，這可能導致我們之客戶減少支出或轉向我們之競爭對手。消費者支出減少可能導致我們產品之需求減少，也可能導致銷售與促銷費用增加。影響消費者支出廣泛之問題或趨勢，可能對我們之會員支出產生不成比例之影響。消費者支出減少或轉移可能對我們之業務、營運成果及財務狀況造成負面影響。

我們依賴擁有大量且忠誠之會員。我們在會員人數及維持高續約率之程度，對我們之利潤率有重大影響。此外，我們之淨銷售額直接受會員人數、持有我們合作品牌信用卡之會員人數、會員於我們俱樂部購物之頻率及於該次購物所花費之金額影響，這表示會員之忠誠度與熱情直接影響我們之淨銷售額與營運收入。因此，任何會損害我們與會員之關係，導致續約率降低或會員於我們俱樂部之支出減少之因素，可能對我們之淨銷售額、會員費用收入及營運成果造成重大不利影響。

可能對我們與會員之關係產生負面影響的因素包括：我們未能相對於競爭對手保持具競爭力之價格；我們未能提供預期之商品品質；我們未能提供會員所期望之商品組合；事件損害我們之聲譽或我們之自有品牌聲譽；我們未能提供會員可能期望之便利性，包括科技、配送及俱樂部實體位置；我們之會員費用提高；以及來自商店、俱樂部或網際網路零售商之競爭增加，這些零售商在價格、品質與便利性之組合上更具吸引力。此外，我們必須持續吸引新會員以取代未續約之會員並擴大會員人數。若我們未能吸引新會員，我們之會員費用收入與淨銷售額可能受損。

我們之業務計畫依賴我們能以最佳價格取得所銷售之商品。由於我們對商品價格採取積極策略，我們銷售某項商品之價格與購入該商品之成本之間之差額，通常遠低於我們非俱樂部競爭對手之情況。此外，我們通常無法透過提高會員之價格來反映我們之商品成本增加。因此，我們購入商品之價格微小變動，可能對我們之營運利潤產生重大影響。若我們無法相對於競爭對手以具吸引力之價格購入商品，我們之成長可能受挫。若我們購入商品之價格提高，我們之營運利潤與營運成果可能受挫，且若我們被迫提高對會員之價格，我們之會員忠誠度可能受挫。

我們嚴重依賴我們能以具競爭力之價格取得足夠數量之商品，且能及時取得。我們從多種國內外供應商處取得商品。尋找符合我們標準之合格供應商，並能及時且有效率地取得商品，是重大挑戰，尤其針對位於美國境外之供應商及來自美國境外之商品來源。我們無法確保持續供應、價格或取得新產品之能力，且一般而言，任何供應商皆可能隨時改變對我們之銷售條款或停止對我們銷售。此外，會員需求可能導致我們商品庫存不足。此外，若重要供應商，特別是供應高需求商品且我們缺乏替代來源之供應商，因任何原因導致供應鏈中斷，而影響其能以及時或成本效益方式供應我們所需商品之能力，此中斷可能對我們之銷售與營運成果產生重大影響，且過去已對我們之銷售與營運成果產生重大影響。
